ideaflow/2026-02-16/consciousness.html.title: consciousness
ideaflow/2026-02-16/consciousness.html.description: consciousnessThe idea of becoming conscious, or, you know, becoming a gentic, or, like, understanding the world around you and yourself, is it interesting that thing that I could probably write about? I think a good framing is like, you know, something like on becoming conscious, right? I think it's fairly understandable, and... the certain things inside are fairly explainable. I think a couple aspects outline what I think I mean by this. One is, like, you know, understand... Sorry. Understanding of yourself, right? There are definitely many tears of this. Especially the world. I mean, that's easier to explain. First, here is, like, what the fuck is the world, right? Like, you're not aware that there is such a thing as, like, an environment and, you know, you're not aware that there's a separation between you and the environment, and you can do certain things. Um... So that definitely kind of ties into, like, the understanding of you, uh, and your relationship to the environment. These are all kind of related. Um, and then there's, uh... a understanding which is like, Oh, yeah, there is an environment, and, you know, you're in it, and you do things, right? And then there's a understanding of like, how does the environment work? Like, what happens when you do certain actions? What happens when other people do certain actions? What happens when other things sue certain actions? Like, are there predictable patterns? And, you know, yes, there are. And then there are higher levels of understanding that are like, what are the dynamics that arise? When there are people like us, and when there are environments such as the one that we have? et cetera. And there are more higher dimensions as well. And then there's, like, the self understanding, and I think self understanding is the most important of, like, self goals as well. Like, you know, like, you're in this world, and you're acting, and you're like, Why am I acting? Like, why do I do the things that I do? Um, is there for some goal or something? Um, I think that's a part of being conscious as well. And then there's kind of, like, opinions, you know, strategies for existing the world and interacting with other people. #towrite

ideaflow/2026-03-18/meditation-calm-afte.description:
meditation/calm after exercise; appreciating life #bold 22:52:52. march 18th, 2026 im biking through stanford on a downwards slope i rush through the wind like a runner full of adrenaline. i am full of adrenaline. speed makes me happy toward the station, i weave on the roads with not a car in sight down the ramp into the tunnel and out i come onto the station im exhausted but energetic i sit on a maroon bench on the south side of the north bound palo alto caltrain station sweating, i take off my glasses, and take my keys and phone out of my pockets. i unbuckle my helmet i plug in my front bike light and sit there while four drops of sweat slide slowly down the sides of my head i move my hands to wipe and then back nothing cars woosh by behind me i close my eyes. leaning into the 120 degree metal grid "back rest" hurts, do i dont instead, i sit up and breathe one deep breath is all that takse for me to become serene a deep sense of pleasure flows through my lungs into my body as i inhale bike light blue flashing; charging brick; backpack and bike and helmet and phone; four lamp posts on the other side with bright lights, unmoving; orange lights are evil twins. train arrives.
#A #experience

qualia-is-the-problem.html.title: qualia is THE problem
qualia-is-the-problem.html.description:
why / how do we have subjective conscionusness? everything else is a tech problemship of theseus: if in a human brain one neuron at a time were replaced by artificial neurons, would this human still be conscious? will a ground truth test of consciousness ever be possible? ofc it seems impossible right now but many things seem impossible but then when someone comes along and solves it in hindsight it doesnt seem so impossible anymore i wonder if good theories of consciousness can approximate a test of consciousness by fitting a rule about whether someone/something is conscious based on the internals critical brain theory Consciousness from qualia research institute complete circuits

Attention and awareness: A two-stroke model of consciousness different older things like iit etc <-> nk networks? interesting modeling representations
cooked: OSF that quantum thing
The mystery of consciousness - Google Slides jason hausenloy and janet or something: predictive processing like thermometers or something i remember this to be pretty convincing split brain continuity? what about sleep? teleporters?? the first thing to do would be tests of consciousness; pretty critically important for humans (to determine if we can do unethical things to them w.r.t. pain) anesthesia for empirical observations increasing communication bandwidth between people <-> fusing consciousnesses "Increasing communication between people is one of the most beautiful things you could do." info_displayTitle.description: Descriptive title to show above the feature

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.

info_allowResizing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be resized

info_allowCollapsing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be collapsed

info_rightDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the right sidebar

info_leftDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the left sidebar

info_selector.description: CSS selector for an element. The feature will be placed relative to this element.

info_type.description: Will this feature be placed before, after, or inside (at the beggining or end).

info_featurePlacement.description: Where to place this feature on the page. (Relative to the selector)

info_sourcePath.description: The local path to the source .html file which will be included.

info_allowFoldingLists.description: Whether or not to allow lists to be folded

info_allowFoldingHeadings.description: Whether or not to allow headings to be folded

info_siteUrl.description: The url that this site will be hosted at

info_authorName.description: The name of the author of the site
